OWNED FILES: frontend/e2e/judge-journeys.js, frontend/e2e/judge-journeys.test.js.

BACKGROUND: buildSceneJudgments(report) computes `revealedKnowledgeIds` for the canon judge from committed reveal evidence: for a turn with `attempt_bundle` it uses attempt_bundle.outcome === 'committed' && attempt_bundle.selected_reveal.knowledge_ids; turns without a bundle fall back to grounding_ids and mark scene.reveal_evidence ('committed_bundles' | 'mixed' | 'grounding_fallback'). BUT real saved reports do not put the bundle on the turn: frontend/e2e/blind-player.js turnLog() emits turns WITHOUT attempt_bundle (it keeps only `outcome` and `transition_cause`), while the SAME scene object carries a separate `bundles` array from collectBundles(): [{turn: <number>, attempt_bundle: {...}}]. So on real reports every turn takes the grounding fallback and the fix has no effect.

CHANGE: in buildSceneJudgments, before computing evidence, attach bundles to turns by joining scene.bundles to scene.turns on the `turn` number (a turn's own inline `attempt_bundle`, if present, wins; a bundle whose turn number matches no turn is ignored; duplicate turn numbers: use the first). Everything else, including rejected-turn handling and the reveal_evidence marker, stays as is. Do not change turn text or any other output field. Add tests: a report shaped like the real one (turns from turnLog shape with no attempt_bundle + scene.bundles) yields committed ids and 'committed_bundles'; a bundle with outcome 'rejected' or 'game_break' contributes nothing; a partial bundles list gives 'mixed'; inline bundle wins over the joined one; unmatched bundle turn numbers are ignored. Also add one test that loads a real saved report pair if present at artifacts/e2e-blind-player.json (+ artifacts/e2e-blind-player-bundles-r1.json) -- skip it when absent -- but ONLY if you can tell from the files how they join; otherwise omit it and say so in your notes.

OWNED FILES: frontend/e2e/helpers.js, frontend/e2e/blind-player.test.js.

BACKGROUND: frontend/e2e/helpers.js resolveWarningIfPresent(page) used to click 'Return to scene' and then `await expect(warning).toBeHidden()` -- it THREW if the panel stayed visible. It is now implemented on top of handleGameBreak (frontend/e2e/blind-player.js), which never throws on a panel timeout and returns a record with outcome 'timeout'; resolveWarningIfPresent returns `record != null`, i.e. TRUE even when the panel never closed, so other callers (scene-walk, canon journeys) would carry on with a stuck panel and fail later with a confusing error.

CHANGE: keep the boolean contract (false when there was no panel, true when it was resolved) but THROW an Error with a clear message ('game-break panel did not close ...' including the record's warning_id and outcome) when the returned record's outcome is 'timeout'. Add a node:test case in blind-player.test.js using the existing fakeGameBreakPage helper that checks: no panel -> false; resolved -> true; timeout -> rejects with that message. helpers.js imports @playwright/test; if importing it in a node test is a problem, test via a small exported pure helper you add (in helpers.js or blind-player.js -- you may only edit helpers.js, so put it there) and keep resolveWarningIfPresent a thin wrapper.
